primitives.name: Spin-Gas Glauber Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: # [1852] Feature Programming for Multivariate Time Series Prediction (arXiv:2306.06252) **Citation:** Alex Reneau, Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu, Chenwei Xu, Weijian Li, Ammar Gilani, Han Liu (2023).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: X: multivariate time series (dimensionless), t: discrete time (seconds), c: scaling constant (dimensionless), σ: spin variables (dimensionless), δt: elementary time step (seconds)
primitives.assumptions: Markovian coin toss increments, spin-gas interaction, coarse-graining limit.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High-noise or non-equilibrium states where the exponential family factorization fails.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's multivariate volatility clustering via Ising spin glass; maps to GSE's event-triggered state transitions through discrete-time Markov chains.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal autocorrelation decay and entropy production rate.

primitives.name: Hammersley-Clifford Spin Glass
primitives.verbatim_quote: Proof in 3 steps: (1) node-conditional (5.7) is a univariate exponential family with sufficient statistics φe(σi,t+δt) = σi,t+δt and canonical Θ = ln(1/2)·Γi,t; (2) with gas-like interaction g in form (5.8), the canonical parameters take the tensor-factorized form (B.4); (3) Hammersley-Clifford + Yang et al.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p(X): joint probability (dimensionless), Z: partition function (dimensionless), V_C: clique potential (Joules), X_C: subset of variables in clique C (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Positive distribution, Markov random field, Gibbs measure, finite-range interactions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Long-range interactions or heavy-tailed distributions violate the local-global correspondence.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's sparse precision matrix estimation via graphical lasso; maps to GSE's contextual action-value functions through Markov decision processes.
layer2.telemetry: Graph connectivity patterns and minimal clique cover size.

primitives.name: Tensor Factorized Canonical Parameters
primitives.verbatim_quote: Proof in 3 steps: (1) node-conditional (5.7) is a univariate exponential family with sufficient statistics φe(σi,t+δt) = σi,t+δt and canonical Θ = ln(1/2)·Γi,t; (2) with gas-like interaction g in form (5.8), the canonical parameters take the tensor-factorized form (B.4); (3) Hammersley-Clifford + Yang et al.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Θ_i: canonical parameter (dimensionless), Γ_i: effective local field (Joules), J_{ij}: interaction tensor (Joules^{-1}), σ_j: spin variable (dimensionless), h_i: external field (Joules), g_i: gas-like term (Joules), p: momentum (kg·m/s), a: acceleration (m/s²)
primitives.assumptions: Exponential family form, linear response to sufficient statistics, tensor product structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-exponential family likelihoods or strong non-linear couplings destroy the factorization.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's generalized linear models with natural gradients; maps to GSE's policy gradient objectives through exponential families of value functions.
layer2.telemetry: Fisher information matrix eigenvalues and KL divergence between conditional distributions.

primitives.name: Difference Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Three operators extracted from the theory: Difference[series1, series2] (first smooth, then subtract; the order-raising building block), Window[series, lookback] (max/min/mean over a fixed lookback, multiple resolutions), Shift[series, Δτ] (arbitrary time displacement).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Δ^{(k)}: k-th order difference (units of X), τ: time lag (seconds), S^{(k-1)}: smoothing operator of order k-1 (same units as X)
primitives.assumptions: Stationary increments, additive noise, finite differencing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-stationary variance or heavy-tailed noise corrupts the differencing.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's volatility extraction via log-differences; maps to GSE's residual value functions through temporal difference learning.
layer2.telemetry: Autocorrelation of differenced series and variance reduction ratio compared to raw data.

Starting with the Hammersley-Clifford theorem, they construct a spin-gas Hamiltonian whose Glauber dynamics generates a Markov process on multivariate time series. The resulting node-conditionals belong to an exponential family with tensor-factorized canonical parameters, which directly yields three primitive operators—difference, window, and shift—as the minimal sufficient statistics for capturing temporal dependencies. This bridges continuous-time stochastic differential equations to discrete-time feature extraction, providing a "compiler" from physical assumptions to algorithmic feature sets. However, the absence of a pruning mechanism means the generated features may include redundant or noisy combinations, and the random holdout validation risks overfitting to idiosyncratic temporal splits.
